name: Acoustic keys
description: Acoustic instruments played through a system of keys.
sound_production: A key transfers the player's gesture to another resonating mechanism.

sections.text: The same key can pluck a string in a harpsichord, launch a hammer in a piano, or open an air passage in an organ.

name: Bowed strings
description: Strings kept vibrating primarily through friction from a bow.
sound_production: The bow repeatedly grips and releases the string, sustaining the sound.

sections.text: A bow sustains vibration and allows a note to be prolonged; fingers can also pluck the string, in a technique called pizzicato.

sound_production: A bow or the fingers set its strings vibrating.

sections.text: Some early cellos had three, four, or five strings. Smaller examples could be supported by a strap and played standing or while moving.

name: Electric bass
description: A low-register electric instrument linked to pulse and harmony.
sound_production: Pickups turn the vibration of low-pitched strings into an electrical signal.

sections.text: The Fender Precision Bass, introduced in 1951, helped make the fretted bass a central part of the pulse in electric bands.

description: An amplified string instrument open to extensive sound processing.
sound_production: Pickups convert string vibration into an electrical signal.

sections.text: The pickup does not produce the sound on its own: it converts string vibration into a signal that can then be filtered, distorted, and spatially processed.

name: Percussion

sound_production: A surface or body resonates after receiving energy.

sections.text: Percussion instruments do not always serve only to keep time. Among the Mexica, the teponaztli took part in religious ceremonies, royal events, military activities, and forms of communication.

sound_production: Each key launches a hammer against a string and releases its damper.

sections.text: Only three pianos built by Cristofori are known today. The 1720 example preserved by the Metropolitan Museum is the oldest of them.

name: Plucked strings
description: A family in which a string vibrates after being pulled by fingers, a pick, or an equivalent mechanism.
sound_production: The string is displaced and released, starting a free vibration.

sections.text: Plucking a string does not require direct finger contact: in a harpsichord, pressing a key raises a small plectrum that plucks the string.

name: Synthesizer
description: An electronic instrument for creating and transforming timbres.
sound_production: Signals are generated or played back, then shaped through controls.

sections.text: The Minimoog popularized the pitch-bend wheel, one of modern music's most notable inventions. It was created specifically so keyboard players could bend the pitch of notes in real time and rival the expressiveness and solos of electric guitars on stage.

name: Acoustic guitar
description: A plucked string instrument with an acoustic resonating body.
sound_production: Strings vibrate when plucked with fingers or a pick; the soundboard and resonating body radiate the sound.

sections.text: The LABEET collection records the acoustic guitar in the ensemble that accompanied lambada in Pará between 1975 and 1978, alongside the carimbó drum, pandeiro, reco-reco, marimba, and banjo. Its presence in the collection extends beyond samba and MPB.

name: Cavaquinho
description: A small plucked string instrument with an acoustic resonating body.
sound_production: Strings plucked with fingers or a pick transmit vibration to the soundboard and resonating body.

sections.text: In the recording of Lapinha de Valdemar from December 8, 1972, cataloged by LABEET, the cavaquinho accompanies the pastoras singers alongside mandolin, acoustic guitar, and pandeiro. The recording documents its use in pastoril, beyond samba and choro settings.

name: Pandeiro
description: A frame drum with a membrane and small metal jingles called soalhas.
sound_production: Strikes and friction excite the membrane; movement of the frame also makes the jingles vibrate.

sections.text: The pandeiro can function as a membranophone when its head is played, or as an idiophone when only its jingles sound as it is shaken. A single instrument brings together two ways of producing sound: a hybrid instrument.

name: Surdo
description: A low-register drum used to mark rhythm in percussion ensembles.
sound_production: Striking the membrane sets the head and the air inside the resonating body vibrating; damping controls the sound's duration.

sections.text: The surdo is placed in ensembles associated with carnival, samba, marchinhas, and samba de morro in Rio de Janeiro. It appears alongside caixa, repique, tamborim, pandeiro, and cuíca, forming a group of membranophones.

name: Tamborim
description: A small single-headed frame drum played with a stick.
sound_production: The stick strikes the membrane stretched over the frame, producing short, defined attacks.

sections.text: Two types of tamborim are distinguished: a handmade type with a deeper wooden body, used in congada and moçambique, and a commercial type with a shallow metal or acrylic frame, common in samba school drum sections.

name: Cuíca
description: A friction drum with a rod attached to the membrane on the inside.
sound_production: Rubbing the rod transmits vibration to the membrane; finger pressure on the head changes the sound.

sections.text: The cuíca appears among the membranophones that accompany the industrially made reco-reco in carnival, samba, marchinhas, and Rio's samba de morro. The record shows its place in ensembles alongside surdo, caixa, and repique.
